headline: This 2020 law directs the Treasury to mint commemorative coins marking the 100th anniversary of the Negro National League, with sale proceeds going to the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum.
what_it_does: The law tells the Department of the Treasury to mint and issue up to 50,000 $5 gold coins, 400,000 $1 silver coins, and 400,000 half-dollar coins. The coins' design must reflect the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum and its mission. Treasury may issue them only during a one-year period starting January 1, 2022, and must run a program to promote collecting them. Surcharges from coin sales go to the museum for educational programs and exhibits.

who_it_affects.how: They can purchase these limited-issue coins during the sales period, with a surcharge on each coin going to the museum.
It receives the surcharge money from coin sales to fund its educational programs, outreach, and exhibits.

who_it_affects.group: The Department of the Treasury (U.S. Mint)
who_it_affects.how: It must design, mint, market, and sell the coins within the set limits and timeframe, and run a promotional and educational program.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted December 4, 2020. Treasury may issue the coins only during the one-year period beginning January 1, 2022.
